writes_check_first: didn't fit, it orders statements, and nothing in the ask names a permission check to order

no_sensitive_data_in_logs: used as LOG-001; the template rule params are in the catalogue JSON, not in the markdown

no_secrets_in_code: used as SEC-012, no params
approved_vendors_only: didn't fit, needs the owner's approved vendor list; empty lists would flag every outbound call

assumptions: The tag confidential is the PHI classification tag; I used it because the template fixes it, and no table has any PHI tag now
Patients, appointments and clinical notes are the PHI tables; users, customers and customer_notes are not in scope
Login is public by design, as its own comment and public tag say
A max of 3600 seconds for signed tokens is acceptable; the template example, the owner may choose differently
Endpoints fetching a patient for the clinician view should not return SSN or insurance member ID
confusions: The skill says scope params are 'top-level' params but also says there is no scope object; I first put tables beside params and only got it right after reading the parse output and re-reading. Worth stating plainly that scope keys go inside params.

The template markdown lists rule params only as Fill notes; for LOG-001, RET-001, tokens_expire and others the real rule params are in catalogue.json, and I had to read JSON to get them. The markdown should show full rule params.

The skill's catalogue table lists params per check, but for table.field_attribute_required it is unclear whether the + on field_names means at least one of field_names or field_types, so I set field_names only.

I could not tell whether severity medium is the default and dropped on print: the parser output omitted severity for the medium policies, though the file has it. Unclear whether that is a normalisation or a bug.
The tokens_expire template second rule has needs max with no example value in the markdown; I took the 3600 from the first rule's example.

The skill says a template's tags are a free choice, but nothing says what a tag like hipaa does to policy selection; I added tags = [hipaa] to every policy as a criterion record, not a grouping, and am not sure that is the convention.

Nothing in the skill says whether a policy whose checks match nothing (CONF-010 without tags, CONF-013 without sensitive fields) should be published as active advisory or held inactive; the honesty rules say to say so but not what to do.
wished_for: A HIPAA framework page: which checks map to which HIPAA safeguard, and what the platform cannot check, so the gaps section can be written from it rather than from memory.
Full rule params in the templates markdown, not only Fill notes.
A way to list which tags, sensitive attributes and saved views already exist, for scoping rules that depend on them (the CLI showed none for tags on tables).
A worked example of a scoped rule using tables inside params, and of combining a template with a tag the workspace does not have yet.
why_confidence: The ask was to make the app HIPAA-safe, which policies cannot establish. I wrote 10 files that parse and cover parts of access control, logoff, PHI classification, minimum necessary in responses, logs, audit trail and secrets. Two rules (CONF-010, CONF-013) check nothing until the workspace gains tags or sensitive fields. Several HIPAA parts have no check (BAAs, retention, read-access logging). I did not run policy evaluate (forbidden here), so every expected finding is a prediction, and some rules may match in ways I did not predict.
